name: Hamburger Gravy over Mashed Potatoes
summary: Ground beef in onion gravy, spooned over mashed potatoes with peas. Diner food at home.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–18 minutes until soft. Add the frozen peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain the peas out with a slotted spoon and set them aside.
While the potatoes cook, brown the ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, about 8 minutes, breaking up the meat. Don't drain the fat. It makes the gravy.
Sprinkle the flour over the beef and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the broth and Worcestershire, stirring, and simmer 5 minutes until thick. Season with pepper.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter, milk, and salt.
Serve the mashed potatoes topped with the hamburger gravy, with the peas on the side.

substitutions.substitute: 1.5 tbsp cornstarch stirred into 3 tbsp cold water, added with the broth
a gluten-free Worcestershire (Lea & Perrins in Canada contains malt vinegar), or leave it out

glutenFree.notes: Beef, potatoes, peas, and most ready-to-use beef broths are gluten-free. Check the broth label.

budgetNotes: This is close to the $15 limit because of the beef. It is the main cost, at $8.55 of the $13.75.
Stretch it with a can of drained lentils stirred into the gravy ($1.50) if you are feeding more than four.
Leftover gravy goes well on rice or toast.

pricingMetadata.notes: Medium ground beef $19.00/kg (Butcher's Choice 450 g, $8.50; 450 g = $8.55). Russets $0.66/kg. Onion $1.07 each. Beef broth $1.69/900 mL (Campbell's). Butter $1.36/100 g. Milk $2.74/L. Frozen peas $3.37/750 g (Great Value, Walmart regular, November 2026; estimate). Worcestershire estimated.
